CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD  AND  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE TYAGARAJA N. INAVALLY  -3-  NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB  MFA No. 200614 of 2024 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)

This appeal is by the claimant filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 10.08.2023 passed by the IV Additional District Judge and MACT-XIII, Vijayapura in MVC No.1026/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 18.06.2019 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.MH-45/U-2604to Nigadi Khurd to attend his personal work.

When he was near the land of Ishwar Dombale, a Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-28/TB-6430 driven by its driver came in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and lost control over it, dashed to the Motorcyclist.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and immediately he was shifted to Civil Hospital, Yalavi and Jath.

Thereafter, he was shifted to Wanless NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR Hospital, Miraj, wherein the petitioner has taken treatment for 16 days as an in-patient and undergone many tests and investigation.
Due to the said accident, his right leg was amputated and accordingly same was operated.
The petitioner has spent nearly Rs.5,00,000/- for medical and other expenses.
3. The petitioner prior to the accident was hale and healthy, aged about 34 years and was doing business and thereby earning Rs.20,000/- per month and maintaining his family.

Due to accident,
he is unable continue his work.
Therefore, the claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
appeared and filed their separate written statement.

Respondent No.1 admitted the date, time and place of accident and denied other contentions of the claim NC:
2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR petition.

Respondent No.2 denied the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the respondent No.1 collided with the police and involved the vehicle in question and further contended that there is violation of policy conditions.

On these grounds,
prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The petitioner, in order to prove the case, examined himself as PW-1 besides Dhanaji vs Surekha And Anr on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150535146/
3 examining the doctor as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely, Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.

On behalf of respondents, one witness is examined as R.W.1 and got marked copy of insurance policy as Ex.R.1.
6.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, as a result of which, the claimant NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,87,840/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
and directed the respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally and respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed seeking enhancement of compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, due to the accident, the right lower limb was amputated, and accordingly same was operated and his daily life is affected.
He has examined the doctor as P.W.2, who deposed that the claimant has suffered disability of 85% to the whole body.
But, the Tribunal has assessed 35% disability to the whole body and the same is on the lower side.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR b)
He further contended that at the time of accident, the claimant was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. by doing business.

However, the Tribunal has assessed notional income of deceased at Rs.13,250/-,
which is on the lower side.
c) Lastly, she has contended that due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injury and he was in-patient for a period of 17 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during the treatment and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other accidental expenses are on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for enhancement of compensation.

8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 - insurance company contend that even though the right leg of the claimant was amputated, the doctor has not deposed that what was exact extent of the disability suffered by the claimant.

Therefore, considering NC:
2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR the injuries suffered by the claimant and medical records, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the whole body disability at 35%.

9. Lastly, he has contended that considering the evidence of doctor and injuries suffered by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities,
other incidental injuries are just and reasonable.
Hence, she sought for dismissal of the appeal.
10. Heard the learned counsel for the parties, perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and also the appeal papers.

4 11.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has suffered injury in a road traffic accident occurred on 18.06.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tractor bearing Reg.No.KA-28/TB-6430.
It is also not in dispute that due to the above accident, the claimant's NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR right lower limb was amputated and to substantiate his claim, he examined the doctor as PW.2.
In his evidence, P.W.2 deposed that the claimant's right leg was amputated and deposed that the disability suffered by the claimant is 85% to the whole body.

Considering the evidence of doctor,
injuries suffered by the claimant, even as per the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, if the amputation of leg below the hip, then 80% disability has to be considered.

In view of the above,
whole body disability has to be assessed at 80%.

12. In the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.13,250/- and also rightly added 40% future prospects to the income of the claimant in view of judgment of Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi And Others [AIR 2017 SC 5157].

assessed as under:
Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injury.
He was in-patient for a period of 17 days.
He has suffered lot of pain during the treatment because of disability and has to suffer unhappiness during his life.

Considering the evidence of doctor and injury suffered by the claimant,
we are inclined to enhance the compensation towards 'pain and suffering' from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-.
The claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities'.
The claimant is also entitled for compensation towards loss of income during laid up period for a period of six months Rs.79,500/- (Rs.13,250/- x 6).
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads are just and reasonable.

14. On re-assessment and re-determination, the computation of compensation is as under:

15. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

- 12 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:6471-DB HC-KAR c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.32,95,060/- as against Rs.14,87,840/-
awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

d) The Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit entire compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
e) The deposit and release shall be as per the order of the Tribunal.
